title: Mitigating Correlated Risk: Framework for Hybrid CSM Deployments and Provider Diversity Scoring
body: Research & Context The Community Staking Module (CSM) has lowered the financial barrier to staking, allowing permissionless operators to spin up nodes. However, infrastructure centralization remains a silent bottleneck. Due to home bandwidth constraints, power grid instability, or upfront hardware costs, a significant cohort of solo operators choose turn-key hosted infrastructure providers (such as cloud VPS providers) rather than hosting physical hardware at home. While hosted providers lower the technical barrier, they introduce severe correlated infrastructure risks. If a single cloud provider or staking-as-a-service host experiences an outage, a large block of Lido CSM validators could go offline or face correlated slashing penalties simultaneously. Conversely, true home staking provides maximum resilience but suffers from lower uptime SLAs. We need a framework that bridges this gap—improving the accessibility of home infrastructure while structuring guardrails around hosted deployments. The Proposal I propose the creation of a CSM Hybrid Architecture Blueprint & Provider Diversity Framework to optimize the risk profile of permissionless operators. This initiative focuses on two distinct areas: 1. The “Fall-Back to Home” (Hybrid) Blueprint We should design and document standardized hybrid infrastructure architectures for CSM operators. Primary/Backup Split: Rather than hosting 100% on a cloud provider, operators are guided to run a low-power, lightweight execution/consensus client pair at home (e.g., using a mini-PC or Raspberry Pi) acting as a passive hot-standby. Automated Failover Guardrails: Open-source scripts that securely migrate validator keys from a failing hosted service to the home setup without risking double-signing (the primary cause of slashing). 2. CSM Provider Diversity Index & “Anti-Correlation” Incentives To protect the protocol, the Lido DAO needs visibility into where CSM nodes are physically running without compromising operator privacy. Voluntary Infrastructure Attestation: Allow operators to optionally sign a cryptographic proof or self-attest to their hosting environment (True Home-Hosted vs. Specific Third-Party Host) during node creation. Dynamic Bonding or Rewards Scaling: Explore long-term tokenomics where operators utilizing highly saturated providers face slightly different bonding requirements or fee structures compared to those contributing to genuine geographic and ISP diversity at home. Expected Impact & Signaling Value Protocol Resilience: Reduces Lido’s vulnerability to systemic cloud provider outages or targeted regulatory pressure on major staking hosts. Onboarding Pragmatism: Acknowledges that pure home staking is not viable for everyone, providing a safe “middle ground” (hybrid) that elevates intermediate operators into advanced decentralized operators. Data-Driven Decentralization: Gives the DAO actionable metrics on the true underlying hardware distribution of the CSM. Next Steps & Community Feedback I would welcome feedback from CSM operators, client developers, and the core team: What open-source tools currently exist that could be adapted for safe, double-signing-protected validator client failovers between cloud and home infrastructure? How can we structurally incentivize operators to choose independent or home-hosted options without creating a punitive environment for beginners?
